subject.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the experimental core Claws status/remove lifecycle, including durable ownership rows and intentional removal without a permanent tombstone, as the direction for the stacked RFC implementation?
rationale: The branch adds a destructive public CLI and durable recovery semantics across agent config, workspace state, sessions, and package ownership; code review cannot choose the permanent product and recovery contract.

options.title: Sponsor the guarded lifecycle
options.body: Approve the experimental ownership and recovery model after the prerequisite stack and complete destructive-path proof are reviewed together.

options.title: Keep status, defer removal
options.body: Retain read-only lifecycle visibility while deferring destructive removal until maintainers choose a durable recovery and retention model.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Leave the series unmerged until the RFC establishes a different lifecycle or ownership boundary.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the guarded lifecycle
recommendation.body: Approve the experimental ownership and recovery model after the prerequisite stack and complete destructive-path proof are reviewed together.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent shared-state, configuration, and filesystem-safety history is the closest current-main ownership signal for the decision.
